policy_title: NHS Staff Retention Plan and Pay Review Body Reform
stated: Train, recruit and retain the doctors, nurses and other NHS staff we need, including by: Establishing a properly independent pay review body, retaining more staff across the NHS through a ten-year retention plan, making flexible working a day-one right and expanding access to flexible, affordable childcare, fixing the work visa system and exempting NHS and care staff from the Immigration Skills Charge, and ending the false economy of spending money on agency workers.

source.quote: Train, recruit and retain the doctors, nurses and other NHS staff we need, including by: Establishing a properly independent pay review body. Retaining more staff across the NHS through a ten-year retention plan. Making flexible working a day-one right and expanding access to flexible, affordable childcare, as set out in chapters 4 and 9. Fixing the work visa system and exempting NHS and care staff from the Immigration Skills Charge, as set out in chapter 18. Ending the false economy of spending money on agency workers and encouraging the use of flexible staff banks.

bearing_set.reason: Retaining more NHS staff, ending agency-worker dependence, and fixing visa routes for NHS and care workers directly affect workforce capacity — the binding constraint on waiting lists, GP access, and overall NHS throughput.

An independent pay review body and day-one flexible working rights materially affect pay levels and working conditions for hundreds of thousands of NHS workers, earning a real verdict on fair pay and job quality.

Ending reliance on expensive agency workers generates a concrete fiscal saving (agency rates are materially higher than permanent staff costs), while exempting NHS/care staff from the Immigration Skills Charge reduces government revenue — the net fiscal effect on the funded/borrowed balance is non-negligible in either direction.

membership_note: The policy's three genuine bearings are: NHS capacity (O3, its primary designed-for outcome), NHS workers' pay and conditions (O4, via pay body independence and flexible working rights), and public expenditure sustainability (O12, via the explicit agency-spend reduction vs. skills-charge exemption tradeoff). Effects on inequality (O14) or prosperity (O13) are too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
